title: Germany to Phase Out Fossil Fuels by 2045
paragraphs: Germany, Europe's largest economy, has made an official pledge to completely phase out fossil fuels by 2045.
On September 23, German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider presented a roadmap for the plan at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
In the roadmap, the German government makes a clear promise to transition away from fossil fuels. Previously, the government had only aimed to be carbon neutral.

To achieve its goals, Germany plans to increase renewable energy from 55% to 80% of electricity generation by 2030. This will be supported by a full phase-out of coal no later than 2038, the expansion of electricity grids, and by switching gas-fired power stations to green hydrogen.
The roadmap also plans for the electrification of transport, heating systems and industrial processes, using technologies such as electric cars for transport and heat pumps for heating.
Schneider said the roadmap not only represents a climate strategy, but an economic policy.

At present, Germany relies heavily on fossil fuels for its energy needs. In 2024, 65% of the country's energy came from oil, gas or coal. Ninety-eight percent of the oil and 95% of the gas were imported at a total cost of $86 billion. But since then, costs have risen even higher because of the war in Iran.
Schneider said that in future, money previously spent on importing fossil fuels would be invested instead in creating locally produced, affordable energy, giving Germany more energy independence.
Schneider said that the German plan could help show other countries how phasing out fossil fuels could be achieved.
"Our road map is intended to set an international example," he told the UN General Assembly. "I am sure that many other countries will follow."
Germany is the third country after France and the Netherlands to present a fossil fuel-free roadmap.
